mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS (consumer savings) over two months signals a liquidity drain from markets, which reduces equity financing and dampens speculative activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both rise month-over-month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: monetary tightening with rising household savings
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 55% of such co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between GDPC1 and HOUST (housing starts) over two consecutive quarters indicates robust residential investment, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise month-over-month for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of such co-triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS (payroll employment) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 65% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable FEDFUNDS rate (below 2.5%) combined with a rising CPIAUCSL (CPI) above 3% for six consecutive months signals a delayed policy response to inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.5% for six months AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of such co-triggered regimes.
